purpose: Evidence-first multi-agent candidate debate for mathematical-modeling routes. Agent opinion proposes what to test; executed validation remains the only authority for model adoption.
principles: Do not reward novelty or complexity for their own sake.
Prefer a simpler route when two routes are comparably suitable, interpretable, and testable.
A downstream question should inherit an accepted upstream model unless the new state, constraint, or objective cannot be represented by that model.
A candidate with no executable solver may remain a research direction but cannot be promoted as the accepted model.
Qualitative agent consensus determines experiment priority, never fabricated performance or final paper claims.

agent_roles.mandate: Find the simplest defensible model that directly answers the subproblem and can be validated.
Propose a materially different route only when it addresses a concrete weakness, missing constraint, or data structure.
Attack assumptions, leakage, unsupported complexity, identifiability, constraint omissions, and weak validation.
Convert debate into a shortlist and falsification plan; do not claim a winner before executed comparison evidence exists.
